question.text: How should the complete agent workspace be designed across code layout, agent architecture, memory, enforcement, and agent-generated user interfaces?
question.scope: the enforcement and memory layers, measured over one continuous session

claim.position: Gates became a real enforcement boundary on 2026-08-05, and the same day showed the boundary's own blind spot. GQ-001 v1 measured that the gates had blocked ZERO pushes and concluded they were 'a pre-commit convention rather than an enforcement boundary'. That no longer holds: a pre-push hook REFUSED an actual push today, correctly, on a genuine 200-book gap between the corpus index and the texts on disk. Every count in v1 has also moved — 6 gates to 11, 14 self-test cases to 15, 2 probes to 8. The sharper finding is what enforcement still cannot see. Five defects fixed today shared one shape the entire gate layer was blind to: the input was ABSENT rather than WRONG, and each checker answered as though absent meant fine. mktemp failed silently so a logfile variable became the empty string, making an OCR-skip branch unreachable and failing a correct corpus. A retention job pointed at a file containing the literal text 'not a database' printed 'rows total: unknown' and then 'nothing to do' and exited 0. A coverage audit reported findings [] with checked_files: 0 — its own output carried the evidence and nothing acted on it. Every self-test case broke artifacts by making them WRONG; not one removed an input entirely, so all five would have passed the suite. Worst, six probes in that suite printed PASS and FAIL into a void: forcing a FAIL still produced '15 passed, 0 failed' and exit 0, because the probes are subshells and the counters lived only in check(). For their whole existence those probes were decorative — the same defect they exist to catch, inside the tool used to catch it. So the limit is not that gates miss what only execution finds, as v1 had it; it is that a gate's INPUT is unguarded. A checker proves nothing about its own reachability, and a verdict nobody counts is indistinguishable from a verdict that passed. Fixed by adding starvation cases alongside corruption cases, making all 8 probes exit non-zero and be counted (23 passed / 0 failed healthy; 22/1 and exit 1 when one is forced), and making three checkers refuse on empty rather than default to zero. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-05T21:37:38Z after this claim's own trigger fired: adding --strict to the eleventh chain entry touched package.json, a watched path, and evaluate-refresh correctly derived STALE against a recorded fresh. The counts are unchanged on re-derivation (11 chain entries, 15 self-test cases, 8 probes) — the chain gained a FLAG, not an entry. The enforcement evidence strengthened rather than weakened: THREE pushes were blocked on 2026-08-05, not one — the rebuild self-test on a genuine 200-book index/disk gap, the load-bearing suite's baseline when a new gate fired 44 times on synthetic history, and this refresh evaluator on the staleness of this very claim. v1's 'the gates have blocked ZERO pushes' is now falsified three times over. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-06T04:05:19Z, trigger 'self-test case count change' having fired: the gate self-test went 22 -> 23 cases. Re-derived: 11 chain entries, 15 check cases, 8 probes (23 total), and gates-are-load-bearing now proves TEN gates rather than nine — evaluate-refresh was the one gate whose removal had never been tested, excluded because a scratch copy could not run it; it now detects unusable history itself and sits in the chain like any other. Pushes blocked across 2026-08-05/06 stands at SIX. The strongest evidence for this claim's own position arrived from its own filters: five filters I added in one day each silently narrowed what a gate could see, and every one was caught by a suite rather than by review. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-06T11:31:08Z after 'self-test case count change' fired: the rebuild self-test went 9 -> 12 cases, covering search ranking, deduplication and the malformed-query exit code — work that had NO test until then. Re-derived: 11 chain entries, 15 gate check cases, 8 probes, 12 rebuild cases. The strongest new evidence for this claim's position came from writing those tests: my first ranking case counted highlight markers and PASSED with an ORDER BY deleted. A test whose name overclaims what it asserts is the same defect as a probe printing into a void — and I reproduced it inside the fix for that very class, one day later. Enforcement catches what it is pointed at; nothing catches a check pointed at the wrong property except injecting the defect and watching. RE-CHECKED 2026-08-06T16:56:47Z after 'self-test case count change' fired: the gate self-test went 23 -> 24 cases, adding a probe over the two rules that decide what enters the corpus — an age-based rights upgrade and a not-a-book filter. Re-derived: 11 chain entries, 15 gate check cases, 9 probes, 12 rebuild cases. New evidence for this claim's limit: BOTH rules were untestable when written, because they lived inside a script that fetches from the Internet Archive at import time. Enforcement cannot reach code that cannot be pointed at a fixture, and this time the unreachable code was the RIGHTS layer — the decision about whether a book may lawfully enter the corpus at all. And placing the new probe above its own counter helper made it run while its result was silently dropped: 23 stayed 23. That is the decorative-probe defect from one day earlier, reproduced inside the fix for a different rule, and caught only because I check that the count MOVES rather than that the suite is green.

source.title: Probes that printed into a void
The guard that could not fire

action.description: Guard the INPUT of every checker, not only its output: starvation cases beside corruption cases, probe verdicts counted, and refusal rather than a zero default when a source cannot be read.

invalidate_on: a push blocked or not blocked by the hook
